text:
sarah: running an nsys trace of the serving runtime in our slim/chroot image and seeing kernel names but no file:line for our inference kernels or CUDA kernels. timeline shows <unknown>:0 for most frames. anyone seen this?

sarah: command I used:
```
nsys profile --output=/tmp/run --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --sample=none --sample-interval=0 --stats=true 
  -- python -m infra/serve --workload smoke
```

miguel: first question: were the binaries built with debug info and not stripped? and which CUPTI/libcupti.so version is inside the image? :thinking:

sarah: build flags we use in CI: `-O2 -march=native -g -fno-omit-frame-pointer` but our packaging step runs `strip --strip-debug` to shrink the distro. base image is debian:slim then we do a chroot copy and a small cleanup. Dockerfile snippet:
```Dockerfile
FROM debian:slim
COPY --from=builder /opt/app /opt/app
RUN strip --strip-debug /opt/app/bin/* || true
# then move to chroot/ minimal layout
```

chloe: stripping in the Dockerfile will remove DWARF so nsys can't map PC->file:line. also with chrooted/relocated binaries the .gnu.debuglink / build-id mapping can break if `/usr/lib/debug` isn't present with the matching debug files. did you check `readelf -n` on the binary for a .note.gnu.build-id?

phil: also watch out for debug path prefix issues if you compiled on a build host then relocated. `-fdebug-prefix-map=/home/runner=/src` helps. and if the container is missing `/usr/lib/debug/.build-id/xx/yyy.debug` nsys won't find the debug info.

sarah: ran `readelf -n /opt/app/bin/worker` and got nothing in the `.note.gnu.build-id`. suspect strip removed it. quick repro output:
```
$ readelf -n /opt/app/bin/worker | sed -n '1,120p'
Displaying notes found in: .note.ABI-tag .note.gnu.build-id
  Build ID: (none)
```

miguel: yep that explains it for host symbols. for CUDA kernels, sometimes CUPTI/libcupti mismatch causes symbolization to fail for GPU kernels. inside the image, run `ldd $(python -c "import cupy; print(cupy._core._get_library_path())")` or `ldd /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so` to check versions. what does `nvcc --version` and the driver version show?

sarah: quick check shows `libcupti.so.12.1` but driver on CI runners is 12.0. I also saw warnings in nsys logs about "CUPTI version mismatch".

dev-tools-bot: internal runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tracing/symbolization — contains tips for container debug mapping, `--mount /usr/lib/debug`, and `-fdebug-prefix-map` examples.

chloe: another trick: keep unstripped binaries in a `/debug` layer and bind-mount `/debug` -> `/usr/lib/debug` at runtime for profiling. or package separate `.debug` files using `objcopy --only-keep-debug` and keep the mapping in `.gnu_debuglink`.

phil: for nsys-specific flags, export the profile to sqlite and use `nsys stats`/`nsys-ui` for symbolization hints. also try `nsys profile --sample=none --trace=cuda` with the unstripped binary mounted, and run `addr2line -e /opt/app/bin/worker 0x7f4a2b3c` on suspicious addresses.

miguel: small note on chroot paths: if you relocated sources at build time (containerized build) then DWARF paths point at original absolute paths that don't exist on the profiler host. `-fdebug-prefix-map=$PWD=/src` during compile rewrites them to portable paths. that fixed us in the past when CI builds ran in ephemeral dirs.

sarah: update after a few runs: rebuilt without strip (kept `-g`), added `-fdebug-prefix-map` and mounted `/usr/lib/debug` into the container. host-user-space symbols now map correctly in nsys (file:line visible). CUDA kernels were still anonymous until I swapped libcupti to match the driver (upgraded container CUPTI from 12.1 -> 12.0 to match runner) — after that GPU kernel frames showed file:line where available. :tada:

sarah: final note — if you see NVTX markers but no file:line for kernels, suspect CUPTI/driver mismatch rather than DWARF. if you see `<unknown>` for host frames, check strip/build-id/debuglink and debug-prefix-map. thanks all for the tips. :pray:
